title: Closed Domain States Represented as Primitive Codes
pattern: An internal closed set of states, categories, or options is stored as raw text, including heap-allocated status tags, or raw string/integer codes drive repeated state-specific business branching.
why_bad: Primitive codes admit invalid values and spelling mistakes (e.g., `"REQEUSTED"` compiles and fails at runtime), and repeated dispatch scatters behavior changes across every inline conditional, violating the Open-Closed Principle. Heap-owned text tags can also introduce avoidable allocation and comparison work, depending on representation and workload.
detection: Subcase A: fields or values representing a known finite set of alternatives remain `String`/`&str` rather than a checked variant type; names such as `status`, `kind`, `category`, `state`, `role`, or `type` are leads, not proof. Subcase B: repeated `if`/`match` dispatch compares raw string or integer codes to domain literals to select behavior. Establish the set's closed nature before recommending exhaustive variants.
source: *Refactoring* by Martin Fowler (p. 286); *Refactoring to Patterns* (p. 166); *Refactoring to Patterns* by Joshua Kerievsky (p. 165); *A Philosophy of Software Design*, Chapter 20 (p. 317); *Code Complete*, Section 25.3 (p. 350).
